subject: Enclave peering, MTU constraints and ops handshake — Brookline private deploy
messages:
From: Max Turner <max.turner@brooklinehealth.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: brookline-network-team@brooklinehealth.com
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy — enclave peering and MTU concerns

Hi Olga,

Thanks for the kickoff yesterday. We're starting to assemble the network runbook for our private deployment and have two immediate asks before we schedule the first engineer walk-through:

1) Brookline's primary edge network enforces a 1400B MTU on transit between racks (old load balancers). We need to confirm Redwood's recommended MTU and whether the enclave peering will tolerate 1400B or require fragmentation/DF handling.

2) Our security team wants to understand the initial ops handshake: how will Redwood manage certs for the private control plane, and what is the expected HSM/KMS integration window (we use Thales Cloud HSM)?

I've attached a firewall export and a high-level topology. Can we get a short checklist of what Brookline needs to produce (IP prefixes, proxy ACLs, jump host access window) so we can collate artifacts on our side?

Proposed meeting windows next week: Tue/Wed mornings PT.

Thanks —
Max
Max Turner
Senior Infrastructure Lead, Brookline Health
max.turner@brooklinehealth.com

Attachments: brookline-fw-export-20281005.csv (CSV), brookline-topo.pdf (referenced)

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: Max Turner <max.turner@brooklinehealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 05 Oct 2028 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — enclave peering and MTU concerns

Max — thanks for the clear notes and the export. Short answers up front:

- MTU: Our runtime supports MTU down to 1400B with a couple of caveats (GRE/encapsulation overhead and jumbo-frame optimization disabled). We prefer 1500B for KV cache replication lanes, but production traffic will work at 1400B if you enable PMTU discovery and don't set DF across the path. We'll include an explicit MTU test in the smoke plan.

- Cert/KMS: For Private we have two supported flows: (1) KMS proxy integration (recommended) where you grant a service principal access to wrap/unwrap keys in Thales; or (2) local HSM provisioning if the environment is air-gapped. For the initial handoff we'll need an envelope-wrapped key policy and service account mapping.

I've sketched a lightweight mutual-action checklist below — please produce the bullet items on the Brookline side so we can book a Day-0 run:

Brookline deliverables (minimum):
- Management prefixes and ASN for BGP peering (primary + failover)
- NAT/egress policy and sample outbound ranges for telemetry egress
- Firewall export (you provided — good) + ACL intent doc
- Jump-host bastion user list (SSH public keys) and approved SSH time windows
- KMS contact and service principal details for Thales integration
- Any deep packet inspection/proxy that terminates TLS (we need cert pinning exceptions)
- A point estimate for peak sustained TPS, avg sequence length, and expected concurrency (we use this for qos/burst sizing)

Redwood deliverables:
- RDW network diagram (attached) and MTU compatibility notes
- Day-0 smoke test plan (MTU, TLS handshake, KV cache sync, cert rotation smoke)
- Signed bootstrap artifacts for air-gapped installs (if needed)
- Canaries/rollback plan and recommended two-hour maintenance window for first cutover

Attachments: rdw-network-diagram-v1.png, redwood-onprem-checklist-v0.9.pdf

Can you confirm the above and share any constraints (e.g., block of IPs can't be used, customer-managed NAT required)? If Tue/Wed morning PT works, let's pick Tue 09:30 PT for a 60-minute technical walk. I'll invite infra, security, and an on-call runtime engineer.

Cheers —
Olga Petrov
Onboarding Lead, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai

---
Note: For MTU verification we'll do an explicit ping-of-death style verification and run a small streaming job to validate KV fragmentation behavior.

From: ben.carter@redwood.ai
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, Max Turner <max.turner@brooklinehealth.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 08 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — enclave peering and MTU concerns

Quick add from infra:

- If Brookline enforces 1400B, we should disable jumbo frames in the inter-enclave replication path and enable our fragmentation-aware kernel. That will add ~2-4ms to cold KV syncs; call it out in the SLO doc.
- Recommend we include an eBPF-based ingress filter for the Day-0 smoke to catch unexpected protocol probes.

Ben
Senior PM, Private Infra
Redwood Inference

On a separate note: I can spare a runtime engineer for the Tue 09:30 PT slot if we lock it in.

From: Max Turner <max.turner@brooklinehealth.com>

Cc: brookline-network-team@brooklinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 09 Oct 2028 08:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy — enclave peering and MTU concerns

Thanks — confirmed items below and a couple of clarifications:

- We can provide management prefixes and BGP ASN; we have a /22 available for management but cannot split without change control.
- Tunnel/encap: we will not allow DF on the transit path by default. We can enable PMTU discovery.
- KMS: Thales team is ready. I attached the firewall export you requested and a note that our proxy will do TLS inspection for outbound web (we can whitelist redwood control-plane).
- Peak: estimate 450 TPS sustained, average seq length 600 tokens, concurrency expected ~60.

Tue 09:30 PT works for the technical walk. Please include the DocuSign MSA link in the invite if possible (security wants an executed MSA on file).

Regards,
Max
